Assert that microdata add up to a published table

Source: R/reconcile.R
ensure_reconciled.Rd

A checkpoint for the step from microdata to a published table: counted (or summed) by the table's dimensions, the microdata must give the numbers in the table, cell for cell. A cell that differs is a sign that the microdata or the table was built from another extract, with another definition, or with an error, and it is found before the next table is built on the same microdata. Returns data, so it can sit in the middle of a pipeline.

Usage

ensure_reconciled(
  data,
  published,
  by,
  value = "n",
  sum = NULL,
  tolerance = 0,
  success_msg = NULL,
  warn_msg = NULL,
  abort_msg = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, a database table (dbplyr, e.g. DuckDB) or an Arrow table or dataset; see Database and Arrow tables.

published

The published table: a local data frame with the by columns and the value column, one row per cell.

by

Dimension columns, as in ensure_matched(): a character vector, optionally named to map names in data to names in published, e.g. c(year = "tid", municipality = "omraade").

value

Name of the column of published holding the numbers. Default "n".

sum

Column of data to sum (tidy-select). If NULL (default), rows are counted.

tolerance

The largest difference that is accepted, for a table rounded or perturbed for disclosure. Default 0.

success_msg

Message shown when the rule holds. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the console names every check that ran, and a description of the check otherwise.

warn_msg

Message shown when cells differ and no abort_msg is set. Defaults to a description of the check.

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when the rule is broken. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

Value

data invisibly, unchanged.

Details

The table is a data frame you give it, with one row per cell: the dimension columns named in by and the number in value. The package does not fetch tables itself; read the table from the statistics bank and pass it in. Dimension columns of the table are converted to the type of the microdata column first, so a year read as text matches a numeric year.

On failure the cells that differ are reported, with the microdata number in data, the table's in published and difference (data minus published). A cell in the microdata that the table does not have is reported with a missing published; a cell in the table that the microdata do not have counts as 0 in the microdata. A cell whose published value is missing, such as one suppressed for disclosure, is not compared, and the message says how many there are.

The reported rows are counts, not persons. The microdata are counted where they live, so only the counts of a database table are fetched.

See also

ensure_stock_flow() for a population account over periods, checkpoints.

Examples

persons <- data.frame(
  cpr  = c("a", "b", "c", "d", "e"),
  year = c(2023, 2023, 2024, 2024, 2024),
  sex  = c("F", "M", "F", "F", "M")
)
published <- data.frame(
  tid = c("2023", "2023", "2024", "2024"),
  sex = c("F", "M", "F", "M"),
  n   = c(1, 1, 3, 1)
)
# The table has 3 women in 2024, the microdata 2
ensure_reconciled(persons, published, by = c(year = "tid", "sex"))
#> Warning: The count differs from the table by year, sex
#> ℹ 1 row
#>   Of 4 cells compared
#>   Difference: total -1, largest -1
#> ℹ The rows:
#>      year sex    data published difference
#>     <dbl> <chr> <dbl>     <dbl>      <dbl>
#>   1  2024 F         2         3         -1
#> ℹ If the table is rounded or perturbed for disclosure: tolerance = <largest accepted difference>
